title: Hard Capitals Quiz: 20 Tricky World Capitals
description: A hard capitals quiz with 20 tricky questions: Dodoma, Naypyidaw, Thimphu, Ngerulmud and other capitals that fool even geography buffs.
h1: Hard Capitals Quiz: 20 Tricky Capitals to Test You
intro: Think you know your capitals? This hard capitals quiz is full of traps. Many of the countries here have a famous city that is not the capital, like Dar es Salaam, Dubai and Shanghai, and others have capitals that changed recently. You will also face smaller nations from the Indian Ocean and the Pacific, such as Comoros, Palau and Papua New Guinea. The questions start with deceptively simple picks, then ramp up to expert level. Each question gives you about five seconds, so there is no time to second-guess. A short explanation after each answer shows why the right city is the capital.

questions.q: What is the capital of the United States?
questions.explication: Washington, D.C. was founded as the capital in 1790 on land taken from Maryland and Virginia.

questions.q: What is the capital of China?
questions.explication: Beijing has been China's capital for most of the past 700 years. Shanghai is the biggest city.

questions.q: What is the capital of Vietnam?
questions.explication: Hanoi is the capital, while Ho Chi Minh City, the former Saigon, is the largest city.

questions.q: What is the capital of Pakistan?
questions.explication: Islamabad replaced Karachi as the capital in the 1960s. It was purpose-built next to Rawalpindi.

questions.q: What is the capital of the United Arab Emirates?
questions.explication: Abu Dhabi is the capital, and Dubai is the best-known city.

questions.q: What is the capital of Cameroon?
questions.explication: Yaoundé is the political capital, while Douala is the economic hub and largest city.

questions.q: What is the capital of Ecuador?
questions.explication: Quito, high in the Andes at about 9,350 feet, has one of the best-preserved historic centers in Latin America.

questions.q: What is the capital of the Philippines?
questions.explication: Manila sits on Manila Bay on the island of Luzon. Nearby Quezon City is larger by population.

questions.q: What is the capital of Tanzania?
questions.explication: Dodoma is the official capital, though Dar es Salaam remains the largest city and main port.

questions.q: What is the capital of Myanmar (Burma)?
questions.explication: The government moved to Naypyidaw in 2005 and 2006. Yangon, formerly Rangoon, is still the biggest city.

questions.q: What is the capital of Belize?
questions.explication: Belmopan became the capital in 1970, after a hurricane destroyed Belize City in 1961.

questions.q: What is the capital of Malawi?
questions.explication: Lilongwe took over from Zomba as the capital in 1975, in the center of the country.

questions.q: What is the capital of Bhutan?
questions.explication: Thimphu is one of the few capitals in the world without traffic lights.

questions.q: What is the capital of Madagascar?
questions.explication: Antananarivo, often just called Tana, lies in the central highlands.

questions.q: What is the capital of Mauritius?
questions.explication: Port Louis, on the northwest coast, is the capital and main port.

questions.q: What is the capital of the Seychelles?
questions.explication: Victoria, on the island of Mahé, is among the smallest capital cities in the world.

questions.q: What is the capital of Palau?
questions.explication: Ngerulmud became the capital in 2006. Koror is the largest city and was the former capital.

questions.q: What is the capital of Brunei?
questions.explication: Bandar Seri Begawan is the capital of Brunei, a small sultanate on the island of Borneo.

questions.q: What is the capital of the Comoros?
questions.explication: Moroni is on Grande Comore, the largest island of the Comoros archipelago.

questions.q: What is the capital of Papua New Guinea?
questions.explication: Port Moresby sits on the southern coast of the island of New Guinea.

faq: Why is it hard to remember some capitals?

Many countries have a well-known city that is not the capital, such as Sydney in Australia, Istanbul in Turkey or Dar es Salaam in Tanzania. Planned capitals, like Brasília and Abuja, and moved capitals, like Naypyidaw, also confuse people. Practicing with tricky examples helps.
Which capital cities were built from scratch?

Canberra, Brasília, Washington, D.C., Islamabad, Abuja and Naypyidaw are all planned capitals built specifically to serve as the seat of government. Many were chosen to be more central or neutral than the largest city. These cities are often more modern in layout than older capitals, with wide avenues and government districts.
What is the capital of Palau?

Palau's capital is Ngerulmud, in the state of Melekeok. The government moved there in 2006 from Koror, the former capital and still the biggest city. Ngerulmud is one of the least populated national capitals in the world. Its government buildings sit in a small complex on a hillside, quite far from the busy streets of Koror.
